_comment: NotebookLM stamps a wordmark bottom-right, a second one centred above the title on the opening card, and a full-frame end card. Positions are NOT hardcoded: the title-card mark sits relative to the title block, so it moved from y=100 with a one-line title to y=50 with a two-line one. Across five units a fixed box hit one, missed one entirely, and on a third stamped our logo over the title text while the original stayed visible above it. So only a SEARCH REGION is configured and the mark is measured per video by shape. A mark is also only covered where it is actually present - NotebookLM omits the bottom-right one on the title card when it shows the centred one.

bottom_right._comment: search_region is (y0, y1, x0, x1) as fractions. fallback is used only if detection finds nothing, and is the box measured from two 1600x900 samples.

centre_top._comment: Sits above the title, so its height varies with the number of title lines. Region spans y 3-32% to cover both observed positions.

encode._comment: Re-encode quality. The overlays force a re-encode, so these settings decide how much of the source survives. crf 20 / veryfast took a 30.8MB source down to 13.6MB - 326kbps to 144kbps - which softens text on slide-heavy content. stillimage is x264's tune for mostly-static frames with sharp edges, which is exactly what these lectures are. Raise crf to trade quality for size, lower the preset to trade encode time for size.

_discover_comment: Whole-frame OCR sweep for placements the two configured regions do not cover. 0.2fps is one frame every five seconds - coarse on purpose, since a full-frame pass is expensive and any mark that persists a few seconds is still caught. Anything found is logged as a warning and covered.

outro._comment: Branded outro concatenated after everything else. Appended last so chapter times and captions still describe the lecture - the outro only lands after the final chapter. The light cut matches NotebookLM's output exactly (1280x720, 24fps), so no scaling is needed; the dark cut is 848x478 at 60fps and would be padded.
